sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate is semantically faithful and deterministic validation is valid. It targets the supplied ship owner, encodes category, canonical oil-tanker applicability, construction-date and strict deadweight conditions, requires both protection statuses as exactly one typed true value only for applicable ships, and avoids accidental non-applicable passes.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the applicability encoding to use the supplied canonical nltl:oilTanker class on the ship (for example, $this a nltl:oilTanker) rather than comparing nltl:shipType to the invented literal "oil_tanker". The COMPLETE dependency contract explicitly declares oilTanker as a direct constraint term, and the candidate currently omits it. Also enforce each protection-status property as an xsd:boolean true value with appropriate single-value/cardinality handling, so contradictory or non-boolean values cannot accidentally satisfy the requirement; retain the existing category, unit-qualified deadweight, date, and strict less-than threshold conditions.

The candidate now includes the canonical nltl:oilTanker applicability class, preserving the prior repair, but it still does not faithfully enforce the two required protection-status results. Add explicit conditional validation for both nltl:entireCargoTankLengthDoubleBottomProtectionStatus and nltl:wingTankProtectionStatus as exactly one xsd:boolean true value when the ship is applicable; the current SPARQL detects missing/non-true values but allows multiple true values and provides no property-level datatype/cardinality encoding. Keep the category A/B, oil-tanker class, deadweight < 5000 TON_Metric, and construction-date >= 2017-01-01 applicability tests, and ensure non-applicable ships are not made subject to unconditional protection-status minCounts.

The applicability logic still has an accidental pass: the sh:or second branch succeeds for every applicable ship without requiring either protection-status property, so remove it or replace it with a single non-applicable alternative plus an applicable branch that enforces both statuses. Preserve the prior oil-tanker class applicability, category A/B, construction-date, strict deadweight < 5000 TON_Metric, and exactly-one xsd:boolean true constraints. Also encode the COMPLETE contract's declared shipType term and its required oil-tanker applicability semantics without reverting to an invented uncontrolled literal, and ensure the conditional structure does not impose protection-status minCounts on non-applicable ships.

The candidate is semantically faithful and deterministic validation is valid. It targets the supplied ship owner, encodes category, canonical oil-tanker applicability, construction-date and strict deadweight conditions, requires both protection statuses as exactly one typed true value only for applicable ships, and avoids accidental non-applicable passes.
